mutations.name: F1 the catch in publishPresence records unconditionally, so a put that outlives its epoch writes presence-refusal state belonging to a later connection: held across stop() it re-plants the record on the stopped endpoint, and held across a rebuild it plants one on the connection that replaced it (heartbeat 2s against a ~5s put timeout, so a rebuild finishing inside that window is the common case, not a corner). This suite imports @cotal-ai/core, which resolves to dist/, so the command builds core first and afterRestore rebuilds it: without that rebuild the tree keeps a dist/ compiled FROM THE MUTANT after the source is restored, and dist/ is gitignored so git cannot be the recovery.
mutations.expectRed: a presence put that settles AFTER stop() does not resurrect the record on the stopped endpoint

mutations.name: F2 the success arm in publishPresence clears the refusal record without the same-epoch settle ordering, so an earlier put that succeeds after a later put's rejection erases the refusal while the bucket still refuses writes. Heartbeats run every 2s against a ~5s JetStream put timeout, so two puts sharing one live epoch is the routine shape, not a corner: the record then says the bucket is healthy while the newest evidence says it refuses every write. Same dist/ note as F1: this suite imports @cotal-ai/core, which resolves to dist/, so the command builds core first and afterRestore rebuilds it after the source is restored.
mutations.expectRed: an OLDER put succeeding late does not clear a newer same-epoch refusal record

mutations.name: F3 inOrder runs each write directly again instead of chaining it behind the presence chain, so setStatus/resetStatus/setCondition/setAttention/setChannelMode/setModel go back to firing their bodies unserialized: two overlapping calls interleave their puts and the record that lands last is whichever call's second put finished last, not the call made last (#636, #2055).
mutations.expectRed: two overlapping status writes land in call order: the later call's puts start only after the earlier call's have settled

mutations.name: F4 stop() no longer waits on the presence chain before publishing offline, so departure is not ordered behind a write already in flight: the offline put can start before an earlier admitted write's put has settled, and an observer can read a live status after the seat departed (#636).
mutations.expectRed: departure is ordered behind a status write already in flight
